messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] rate_limit_exceeded Ark Systems (ark-prod-vpc) -> 429 spike observed on dedicated pool 'ark-dedicated-1'. 1200 req/min over last 2m. Paging oncall: @oncall-mike
Sasha-ops: saw alert, paging in. I'm on it, grabbing logs + pool metrics
oncall-mike: oncall here — ack. Sasha please paste pool metrics, also notify CS (Anita) and platform (David)
Sasha-ops: pulling metrics now. command: ```rictl pool metrics --pool ark-dedicated-1 --last 5m --granularity 30s``` output: peak util 98%, qlen spikes, token rate 3.2k/min, many 429s with error_code RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
Sasha-ops: also seeing a single tenant id  ark-tenant-77 generating 68% of requests in last 3m
Taylor-se: is that tenant traffic expected? any rollout or batch jobs?
Anita-cs: Ark support just msged: they have a batch run that started unexpectedly. Customers are reporting failures in production, high severity (payment flows). Need ETA asap
David-platform: checking routing/isolations. Pool shows no node failures; it's saturation. We can either isolate tenant or request temporary quota bump (emergency lift) for Ark. Isolation would be faster to stop blast.
Kevin-engr: +1 on isolation. We have an isolation route available: move ark-tenant-77 to a throttled queue or attach per-tenant rate-limiter. How fast can we apply?
Sasha-ops: we have two mitigation knobs: 1) apply per-tenant hard throttling via firewall rule (fast) 2) create temporary capacity by binding an extra burst node to pool (requires approval for emergency capacity)
Oncall-mike: run the quick isolation. Sasha can you apply a tenant throttle to reduce ark-tenant-77 by 75% for now?
Sasha-ops: executing command: ```rictl tenant throttle --tenant ark-tenant-77 --pool ark-dedicated-1 --rate 500r/m --duration 30m --reason "emergency mitigation"```
Deploy-bot: request accepted, action queued. Job id: 8f3a2c.
Sasha-ops: throttle applied. Observing metrics...
Sasha-ops: 1m after throttle: pool util down to 74%, 429s reduced by ~60%, Ark support says downstream failures reduced but still some error reports
Anita-cs: relaying to Ark: we applied a temporary throttle to the noisy tenant to stabilize the pool. They've acknowledged and asking for a faster long-term fix; can we offer a short emergency lift so Ark's gateway can finish the batch?
David-platform: emergency lift would increase contract throughput for Ark account across their dedicated pool. That requires approvals from finance/agreements for temporary overage. What are the exact numbers they want?
Taylor-se: Ark asked for a 3x rate window for 2 hours to finish their job. If we do that, we still risk other tenants. We should only allow it if we can spin up a temporary isolated burst node and route Ark traffic there. That avoids impacting others.
Kevin-engr: I can provision a burst node labelled ark-burst-1 and bind it to the pool as a soft-fallback for only Ark's tenant id. Provisioning estimate ~8-12min.
Sasha-ops: Meanwhile, we have a shorter option: issue a scoped emergency override token that increases Ark's per-second quota but caps aggregate tokens. That is faster (1-2min) but it's less isolated.
Oncall-mike: decision needed: isolation throttle + provision burst node (preferred) OR scoped temporary override (faster). Anita, what does Ark want?
Anita-cs: Ark prefers fastest path that restores payment flows. They said 2hr lift is ok. They trust us to minimize blast radius. If provisioning time is 10min they can wait. They prefer isolated burst node.
David-platform: approve provision of burst node for 2hr window. I'll tag finance/agreements — we need an emergency invoice note.
Sasha-ops: kicking off provision: ```rictl pool attach-burst --pool ark-dedicated-1 --node-label ark-burst-1 --capacity g4dn.xlarge --exclusive-for tenant ark-account-123 --duration 120m```
Deploy-bot: provisioning started -> node-id nb-0a9b. ETA ~9m.
Sasha-ops: while provisioning, keeping throttle in place to keep steady state. Monitoring logs.
Sasha-ops: 5m mark: queue length stable, 429s down 85%. Ark confirms customer-facing errors dropped from major outage to minor degradation.
David-platform: finance, please note emergency capacity attached to Ark account for 120m. tagging @emma-fin assuming someone from finance will follow up for billing.
Kevin-engr: provisioning complete. Attach completed. Now creating route rule to direct Ark traffic to ark-burst-1 node only for their account id. ```rictl routing add --pool ark-dedicated-1 --match "tenant==ark-account-123" --target ark-burst-1 --priority 10```
Deploy-bot: routing update applied.
Sasha-ops: Ark traffic now on burst node. Pool util for primary nodes down to 42%. Burst node util 65%. No 429s observed for Ark in last 30s.
Anita-cs: Ark support: "Huge improvement — batch finishing. Thank you." They've asked for confirmation when we tear down the burst node.
Oncall-mike: leave throttle off? We should keep it until we confirm batch done. Sasha, recommended plan: keep throttle for additional 10m after Ark reports finished, then remove throttle and drain burst node, then detach node and mark incident resolved.
Taylor-se: also create follow-up ticket to evaluate why batch started unexpectedly and recommend per-tenant quotas or alerts to Ark.
David-platform: agreed. I'll create post-incident action items (PIA): verify autoscaling triggers, per-tenant guardrails, and faster provision path for burst nodes.
Sasha-ops: timeline for closure: wait for Ark confirmation + 10m grace. Noting mitigation steps in incident log.
Anita-cs: Ark confirmed at +22m: batch complete, no errors. They request we remove burst and revert to normal traffic.
Sasha-ops: removing throttle: ```rictl tenant throttle remove --tenant ark-tenant-77 --pool ark-dedicated-1``` -> done.
Sasha-ops: detaching burst node: ```rictl pool detach-node --pool ark-dedicated-1 --node nb-0a9b --drain 60s``` -> completed. Pool metrics stable.
Deploy-bot: node nb-0a9b removed from pool.
Kevin-engr: will run quick post-mortem: initial cause looks like an un-scheduled batch from Ark's side, but internal guardrails didn't catch the sustained ramp until pool saturation.
David-platform: tagging this as SEV2 -> final severity may be lowered after PIA. Noting emergency capacity used and finance follow-up required.
Anita-cs: capturing customer impact: Ark had payment flow degradation for ~18min, then stabilized. They appreciate transparency and we offered a credit check.
Oncall-mike: incident resolved. Good job. Closing thread and creating incident ticket: INC-ark-2061123456.
incident-bot: Incident closed by oncall-mike at 2061123959. Severity: SEV2. Links: /incidents/INC-ark-2061123456
Sasha-ops: adding final note: recommend adding a per-tenant RPS anomaly alert and a faster pre-approved burst workflow for enterprise customers to avoid manual finance approval next time.
Taylor-se: +1 to pre-approved emergency bundles for enterprise customers with simple opt-in.
Anita-cs: I'll follow up with Ark AM to review billing and post-incident notes.
Kevin-engr: will draft PIA and share in #postmortems by EOD.
Oncall-mike: thanks team.
